Overview of Middlesex County Family Court

Middlesex County Family Court is located in New Brunswick, New Jersey, and has jurisdiction over cases arising in Middlesex County. The court handles a wide range of family-related legal matters, including divorce, child custody, domestic violence, and child support.

The family court process in Middlesex County begins with the filing of a case. Once a case has been filed, pre-trial procedures, such as discovery and motion practice, may take place. The trial process itself typically involves the presentation of evidence and witness testimony, with a judge making a final decision on the case.

In Middlesex County Family Court, parties may choose to represent themselves or hire an attorney. Representing oneself can be a challenging and complex process, and it is strongly recommended that individuals seek the assistance of an attorney if they are facing a family law matter.

Mediation in Middlesex County Family Court

Mediation is a process in which a neutral third party helps disputing parties reach a mutually acceptable resolution to their conflict. In Middlesex County Family Court, mediation is often used as a way to resolve family law matters without the need for a trial. The benefits of mediation include a faster and less expensive resolution, as well as increased control over the outcome of the case for the parties involved. The mediation process in Middlesex County Family Court typically involves an initial meeting between the parties and the mediator, followed by negotiations and the drafting of a settlement agreement.

Alternative Dispute Resolution in Middlesex County Family Court

In addition to mediation, Middlesex County Family Court also offers alternative dispute resolution options, such as arbitration and collaborative law. Arbitration is a process in which an arbitrator makes a binding decision on a case, while collaborative law involves both parties working with their attorneys to reach a mutually acceptable resolution. These alternative dispute resolution options can provide a quicker and less adversarial resolution to family law matters than a trial.

Appealing a Decision in Middlesex County Family Court

In some cases, parties may choose to appeal a decision made by Middlesex County Family Court. To do so, they must show that there was an error in the trial process or that the decision was unjust. The appeal process typically involves the submission of written arguments and a hearing before a higher court.
